text:
Leah: Quick feedback needed on the 'mini tour' we show after signup — should it be inline hints that appear once, or a persistent helper pill? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/new/minitour

Diego: Inline hints are less noisy but easy to miss. Helper pill increases discoverability.

Harper: Accessibility: if we use hints, ensure they are linked to elements via aria-describedby; also provide a 'read all' accessible panel.

Vik: From eng: pill is easier to implement (toggle + local storage). Inline hints require element anchors and can break with layout changes.

Leah: Copy thought: top-line 'Need a quick tour?' CTA 'Show me' — softer than 'Start tour'. Include time estimate '1 minute'.

Diego: Also propose showing the pill only for first 3 sessions and then auto-hide; track `minitour.shown` / `minitour.completed`.

Harper: For screen readers announce when the tour opens: 'Mini tour opened. Step 1 of 4.' and add 'Skip tour' button.

Vik: I'll add a feature flag `onboard.minitour_pill` and a lightweight endpoint to record completion. Debounce writes.

UXAssistBot: Suggestion: A/B test pill vs inline hints for conversion to 'create first project' metric.

Leah: Great. I'll update the figma with pill copy and a11y notes, then tag @Vik for spike. Thanks all.
